summary: Ngawang Samten is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Lati Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Tsering, Jampa Yeshe, and Konchok Tsering. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1987-2021, serving as Director), Smith College, Hampshire, Amherst College, and the University of Tasmania.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet works in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University, attested in 2012 under doctoral supervisor Inder Mohan Singh, and also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She pursued doctoral studies at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann, attested in 2013.

Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 2009, under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor K. T. S. Sarao.

Nianzu Huang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932-1936) and under Nordan Hutuktu, Gongga Rinpoche, Hsu Yun, Lianju Xia, and Jiaqi Wang. He held posts as head at Central People's Broadcasting Station and professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.
Nichidatsu Fujii was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Rissho University and founded Nipponzan Myohoji.

Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Ceylon (~1962-1978) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1982-1986).

Nicholas J. Allen was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Rugby School and the University of Oxford (~1969-1976). He held posts at SOAS (1969-1971), Durham University (1972-1976), Wolfson College, Oxford (~1976-2006), and the University of Oxford (~1976-2001).

Nicholas Poppe specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (~1916-1921), he held posts there (~1925-1941), at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1923-1941), the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1930-1941), and the University of Washington (~1949-1968).

Nicholas Roerich was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1893-1898) and the Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts (~1893-1897).
Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (until 2015) and held a research fellow post at the University of Tokyo, attested in 2017.
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Di Cosmo works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Indiana State University and Indiana University (~1985-1991). He held posts at Cambridge (~1989-1992), Harvard (~1993-1999), Canterbury (~1999-2003), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~2003).
Nicolas Morrissey specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012-2013) and under Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, Peter Masefield, Kannika Wimonkasem, and U-tain Wongsathit. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

Nicolas Tournadre specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (-1992) and Paris 8 University (-2002). He held posts at Paris 8, LACITO, INALCO (~1992-2004), University of Virginia (~2000-2004), University of Provence (~2004-2011), and Aix-Marseille University (~2012).

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She held positions at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1958-1971), École du Louvre (~1966-1976), and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1971-1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Østre Borgerdyd school and the universities of Copenhagen, Bonn, Paris, London, and Oxford. In 1845, he became Professor für Indisch-orientalische Philologie at the University of Copenhagen.
Nigel Allan specializes in history and archaeology. Attested in 1993, he succeeded Marianne Winder and held the post of Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust.
